narrative.overview:
The page is a printed transit sheet. Each project is a line in a full-saturation colour, each stop is a real step in that system, and each dotted branch is a real failure path. Everything else exists to read that network: near-black ink on a white enamel sheet, heavy grotesque type, hairline rules instead of containers, and square-framed screenshots as the only imagery of the work.

The density changes on purpose. The first viewport is one diagram edge to edge, then each line takes over the full width as a solid colour band, then the system narrows to ruled rows and strip diagrams for the detail. The page ends on the only ink ground in the system, where all seven lines run down into one terminus.

Arabic and English are equal readings of one sheet. The map mirrors so that trains run in reading direction, the layout uses logical properties throughout, and the bilingual station sign holds both scripts in every locale.
keyCharacteristics: One white sheet, one near-black ink, seven line colours that own whole bands.
A single map geometry, authored once on a grid and derived for right-to-left and portrait.
A fixed station grammar: station, interchange, terminus, dotted failure branch, numbered bullet.
Flat surfaces, square rectangles, circles reserved for the network.
One authored motion family, all of it telling the same story of a line lighting up.

rules.name: The One Colour Per System Rule
rules.body: A line colour identifies one project. Do not use it to decorate another project's content. Two global hovers borrow from the set and are the only exceptions: the hero Email action fills with Line 1 red, and links and the submit button on the ink ground turn Line 4 orange.

rules.name: The Paired On-Colour Rule
rules.body: A line colour never appears behind text without its own on-colour. Orange takes the dark on-colour and is never used for text on white.

rules.name: The Two Grounds Rule
rules.body: White is the ground for the whole page. Ink becomes a ground only at the terminus, where the lines end.

rules.name: The Latin-Only Tracking Rule
rules.body: The -0.03em tracking on display type applies only under `:lang(en)`. Arabic display type is always set at 0, because letter-spacing breaks the joins between Arabic letters.

rules.name: The Arabic Room Rule
rules.body: Arabic gets more leading than Latin: 1.8 for body against 1.6, 1.3 for tracked display against about 1.05, and 1.22 for the hero, whose size also drops from 4.2cqw to 3.7cqw.

rules.name: The Catch-All Fallback Rule
rules.body: `adjustFontFallback` stays false on both fonts. The generated metric fallback is a catch-all Arial with no script range, which sits ahead of Alexandria in the stack and swallows every Arabic glyph. With it off, Arabic falls through to Alexandria as the page intends.

rules.name: The Single Sheet Rule
rules.body: The map is authored once, left-to-right and landscape. Arabic and portrait are derived from it by calculation: transpose first, then mirror x against the view width. Label sides flip with the mirror. Never draw a second geometry.

rules.name: The Octilinear Rule
rules.body: Every map segment is horizontal, vertical or a true 45-degree diagonal. New stops go on the grid.

rules.name: The Flat Enamel Rule
rules.body: A shadow here is a ring: no offset, no blur.

rules.name: The Square Sheet Rule
rules.body: If it is a surface it has square corners; if it is round it is part of the network.

rules.name: The One Motion Rule
rules.body: The network is the only thing that moves: line isolation, the train, the draw-on of the lines at load, and the strip fill. There are no scroll reveals, parallax or entrance effects on text or images. Everything else is a state transition of 150 to 220ms.

rules.name: The Fixed Sign Rule
rules.body: English stays left and Arabic stays right in both locales, as a physical sign does. Each name carries its own `lang` and `dir`, and the current locale's name is the heading. Below 768px the sign stacks with the reader's language first, then the rail, then the other script.

rules.name: The Dash Means Failure Rule
rules.body: Dotted and dashed marks belong to the failure family and nothing else: failure branches and held rings on the map, the dashed outline on strip stops, and the dashed bullet in the When It Goes Wrong list.

dos: Do keep each line's colour paired with its on-colour through `--line` and `--on-line`.
Do add a new project as a new line on the grid, with stops and failure branches that are real.
Do place every map point on the 40 by 21.5 sheet and let the code mirror and transpose it.
Do set the Latin -0.03em tracking through `:lang(en)` only, and give Arabic its own leading.
Do keep `adjustFontFallback` false on Schibsted Grotesk and Alexandria.
Do frame screenshots with the 1.5px ink ring at square corners and native ratio.
Do keep English left and Arabic right on station signs in both locales.
Do use ruled rows for structured detail.
Do honour reduced motion for anything that moves.
donts: Don't add card surfaces, gradients or monospace type; the world has none.
Don't open on a dark hero, set the name in a gradient, or show a grid of technology icons.
Don't present the career as alternating timeline cards; it is a line with stops.
Don't add a line colour without adding a line, or borrow one as general decoration.
Don't set text in Line 4 orange on white.
Don't use dots or dashes for anything other than failure paths.
Don't use a shadow with blur or offset, or round a rectangular surface.
Don't draw separate maps for Arabic or portrait.
Don't add motion outside the network.
